detail: Subsequent work introduced [Sparse Radiance Field (SRF) Representation](8876-sparse-radiance-field-srf-representation.md) to handle irregular volumetric data more efficiently than dense grids. [Mega-NeRF Spatial Partitioning](8776-mega-nerf-spatial-partitioning.md) extended spatial partitioning to large-scale scenes by assigning distinct MLP weights to geometric regions. [MultiPlaneNeRF](8875-multiplanenerf.md) shifted focus from implicit encoding to explicit 2D image projections to improve generalization. [ProNeRF](9673-pronerf.md) introduced projection-aware sampling to reduce the number of required samples. [Quadri-Plane Radiance Fields](11128-quadri-plane-radiance-fields.md) leveraged 2D feature planes to enable efficient super-resolution. [NeRF-XL](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-73195-2_6) provided a framework for scaling these representations across multiple GPUs by sharing specific components like the color MLP while partitioning others [S1].

The evidence source [S1] only discusses the multi-GPU training strategy for scaling NeRF representations (specifically mentioning Instant-NGP as an example). It does not contain information regarding the specific claims about Sparse Radiance Field (SRF), Mega-NeRF, MultiPlaneNeRF, ProNeRF, or Quadri-Plane Radiance Fields. Therefore, while the claim about NeRF-XL is supported by the text, the other facts in the claim are not present in the evidence.
